LESSON: COMPASS DIRECTION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Compass Direction
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

Welcome to this lesson on Compass Direction. In Kenyan schools, learners explore this topic to understand how it connects to daily life in our communities. A key question we explore is: 1.0 Natural and Built Environments

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

B. use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map,

   This means you can explain this in your own words, give a Kenyan example, and show how it applies in school or at home.

C. appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life.

   This means you can explain this in your own words, give a Kenyan example, and show how it applies in school or at home.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Understanding Compass Direction

A. use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map,

   In Kenya, teachers guide learners to observe, discuss, and practise this outcome. Think about your county, school, or home area when studying this point.

At home with your parent or guardian:

1. Discuss what you learned about Compass Direction and share one example from your community.
2. Write three short sentences explaining the main ideas from this topic.
3. Draw or list Kenyan examples that relate to this lesson.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES AND VALUES

Core Competencies:
● Digital Literacy: Learners interact with digital devices as they play computer games on compass direction for enjoyment.

● Learning to learn: Learners develop relationships as they share resources and practise giving direction of places

using the four cardinal points.
